[Ordering verified by Milo (AI), session PRISM_QUEST, 2026-07-28, authorized by TQ: the dependency DAG was checked against the step prose and found complete -- eight of nine steps are data-ordered; the two free steps are true starts: KYC identification (1) and DID/key publication (5), which genuinely precedes verification rather than issuance. orderingAsserted: true.]  [Identity-contract migration applied by Milo (AI), session WILD_ORBIT, 2026-07-29, per workOrder-identityPhase2-072926 (supervisor BRONZE_LOOM): 18 CEDS space-form identifiers normalized to C-form shorthand; 3 prose standard values normalized to registry keys (W3C-VC x2, W3C-DID x1) and 2 to OpenBadges; the four orphan bench products (holder-identity-verification-result, vc-delivered-to-holder, holder-review-decision, wallet-stored-credential) reclassified kind:intermediate. longName: Issue a Learning and Employment Record to a Holder's Digital Wallet
scope: One Issuer issuing one LER to one Holder's wallet. PROPOSED — the issue states no scope; this is the boundary its narrative implies.

keyConcepts.definition: The three-party structure of verifiable-credential exchange: an Issuer who asserts, a Holder who keeps and presents, and a Verifier who checks — supported by registries that supply identity, skill definitions, and trust signals.
Learning and Employment Record. Here, a single micro-credential assertion (an OpenBadge v3) wrapped in a Verifiable Credential and delivered to a learner's digital wallet.

openIssues: No trigger is stated in the source issue — unsurprising, since the issues were written before this standard made the trigger a required slot. The value below is PROPOSED from the issue's own framing and awaits author confirmation.

Step 5 is an OPTIONAL main-path step ('if using a record/trust registry'). The standard inherits spec Issue C: kind/branchesFrom/condition machinery is built for deviations that branch from a main step, not for a main step that sometimes does not happen. Rendered as a main step carrying a condition.

Verification — the Verifier's half of the Trust Triangle — is out of scope here. Nothing in this case consumes the published issuer key, which is why step 5 is unordered (see below). A companion LER Verification case would consume it and would order it.
The issue's Key Concepts section is empty; the two concepts above are PROPOSED from the Introduction and Scenario prose.

actors.role: Issues the LER into the Holder's wallet.
actors.interest: A Holder's digital wallet receives a valid LER.

actors.role: Receives, reviews, and stores the LER.
actors.interest: As a learner and worker, my wallet receives and stores an LER I can present later.

actors.role: Provides identity verification for the know-your-customer step.
actors.interest: Identity assertions it supplies are relied upon correctly.

actors.role: Provides skill definitions and their metadata, addressable by globally unique URI.
actors.interest: Credentials cite registered skill definitions rather than free text.

actors.role: Publishes the Issuer's DID and public key as a trust signal.
actors.interest: Verifiers can later confirm the Issuer's signature.

interestedParties.interest: Can rely on the credential later without re-testing or re-training the worker.

triggeredBy.name: Issuer determines that a Holder has earned a credential

assumes.statement: The learner/worker as Holder has a digital wallet or passport application able to receive the LER.
The Issuer controls a signing key pair and a resolvable decentralized identifier.
The skill or competency being asserted has a registered definition addressable by a globally unique URI.

condition.statement: The Holder's wallet holds a stored, verifiable LER; the learner/worker is empowered with their data as verifiable credentials.
No unsigned or unverifiable credential is delivered to the Holder's wallet; a failed issuance leaves the wallet unchanged.
Every claim in the issued credential cites a registered skill definition by globally unique URI rather than free text.

valueDriver.title: Learner data portability
valueDriver.motivation: A learner and worker holds and carries their own verified record, rather than depending on an institution to re-issue it on request.

valueDriver.title: Eliminate redundant re-training
valueDriver.motivation: Verifiable evidence of demonstrated proficiency lets a later employer accept what has already been proven.

story.action: identifies the Holder by performing know-your-customer (see KYC use cases)
story.intention: the Holder is verified before issuance
story.benefit: so that the credential is bound to the right person

produces.name: Holder Identity Verification Result
produces.role: the verified identity of the Holder, to which claims will be bound

story.action: generates the credential: creates a digital document with specific claims linked to a registered skill definition

consumes.name: Holder Identity Verification Result
consumes.role: the subject the claims are about

story.action: includes a globally unique URI for a registered skill definition and its metadata (e.g., registered proficiency level)
story.intention: claims are anchored to an authoritative skill
story.benefit: so that a later verifier reads the same skill the issuer meant

story.action: digitally signs the VC using the Issuer's private key
story.intention: the credential is tamper-evident and attributable to the Issuer

produces.role: the signed VC envelope carrying the award

story.action: publishes the Issuer's DID and public key for future verification, or attaches verifiable linked credentials
story.intention: verifiers can later confirm the signature

produces.role: the published issuer DID document carrying the verification key

story.action: securely transmits the signed VC to the Holder (e.g., via QR code or direct link)

produces.name: Credential Delivery Event
produces.role: the fact of delivery to a specific Holder

story.action: receives the VC and reviews the claims
story.intention: the Holder validates the credential before storing
story.benefit: so that the Holder keeps only records they recognize as their own

consumes.name: Credential Delivery Event
consumes.role: the delivered credential presented for review

story.action: stores the VC in the digital wallet for future use
story.intention: the credential is retained and presentable

scenario.condition: the Holder does not recognize the claims as their own

story.action: declines the credential and reports the mismatch to the Issuer
story.intention: an incorrect credential is not stored
